description: Biomedical Informatics students at Nile University tackling the astronaut health monitoring challenge. ASTRA compares each astronaut to their own baseline (HR, HRV, sleep, SpO2, activity), detects slow changes early, and tells them what changed, what to do, and when to call the flight surgeon. We bring health data, Python, explainable AI and backend skills. Looking for: Flutter/web frontend, UI/UX (Figma), data visualization, or space medicine/pitching experience.
summary:
ORBIT TWIN is a tablet web app that gives every astronaut a personal health "digital twin": a body map that turns wearable readings and short daily check-ins into clear statuses (Normal, Watch, Act or Unknown) for seven body systems, from heart and brain to bones and radiation.

On deep-space missions, the doctor is no longer one call away. A message to Mars takes up to 20 minutes each way, and contact can stop for two weeks during solar conjunction. ORBIT TWIN runs fully on board with no internet, compares each reading with the astronaut's own pre-flight baseline, and explains every change in plain language with clear "do this now" steps. A medical report then travels to the flight surgeon on Earth with the real light-time delay.

Built on NASA Human Research Program hazards and risks, it helps crews catch slow health changes early and act immediately, keeping astronauts healthy and mission-ready far from Earth.
details:
Written for: the Space Apps judges. The SI answer is only for the organizers' records.

1. Project Details

The box is a rich-text editor, so paste this and add bold to the headings if you like.

WHAT IT DOES
ORBIT TWIN is a tablet web app that gives each astronaut a personal health "digital twin". A body map shows seven body systems (brain, eyes, heart, blood, muscles, bones, radiation), each marked Normal, Watch, Act, or Unknown. Tapping an organ shows today vs. the astronaut's normal, a 30-day trend, and four plain-English answers: what changed, why it matters, how serious it is, and what to do.

HOW IT WORKS
1. Data in: a simulated smartwatch sends heart rate and SpO2 every 5 seconds; sleep, exercise, and a radiation dosimeter add daily values. At a short daily check-in, the astronaut enters blood pressure, temperature, blood sugar, a grip test, a near-vision test, mood and symptoms.
2. The twin compares every value with that astronaut's own pre-flight baseline, using fixed, explainable rules based on NASA Human Research Program risks. Urgent symptoms (e.g., chest pain) raise "Act" even when numbers look normal. A missing reading always shows "Unknown", never "Normal".
3. On board: an "Act" status opens a full-screen alert with "do this now" steps and a button to notify the Crew Medical Officer.
4. Earth later: a Medical Report Packet travels to the flight surgeon with the real one-way light delay (ISS 0.5 s, Moon 1.3 s, Mars about 18 min). The surgeon replies and decides fitness for duty; mission management sees only that decision, never medical details.

BENEFITS
- The crew can act immediately instead of waiting 40+ minutes for an answer from Earth.
- Slow changes are caught early, because each person is compared with their own normal and trend.
- Clear colours and plain language that non-doctors can use.
- Works fully offline, including during the two-week Mars solar-conjunction blackout (Earth-Independent Mode).
- Medical privacy is enforced by the server.

INTENDED IMPACT
Keep astronauts healthy and mission-ready on long missions where Earth cannot answer in time, support the onboard medical officer, and give Earth a complete picture despite the delay. The same idea could help people in remote places on Earth: Antarctic stations, ships, and isolated clinics.

TOOLS AND TECHNOLOGIES
- Languages: TypeScript, JavaScript, HTML, CSS
- Front end: React 19, Vite 6, React Router 7, Tailwind CSS 4, Recharts, Lucide icons
- Server and database: Node.js 22 with built-in SQLite
- Security: hashed PINs, signed session cookies, role-based access
- Offline: service worker
- Testing: 114 automated checks
- Hardware: one laptop or tablet; the watch, cuff, thermometer, glucose meter, and dosimeter are simulated

HOW IT IS CREATIVE
- A "digital twin" of each person, not a generic dashboard: your own body, compared with your own normal.
- Crew Pulse: one private daily question ("Does Ahmed seem like their usual self today?") catches mood changes people miss in themselves. Only counts are shared, never who said what.
- The light delay is part of the design: messages show "on its way" and "arrives in 18 min", just like a real Mars mission.
- Future Slider: shows how bone, muscle, and radiation could change over the mission with and without the exercise plan, clearly labelled as an illustration, not a prediction.

FACTORS WE CONSIDERED
- Safety: emergencies are never delayed; missing data is never shown as healthy.
- False alarms: tested on 1,000 simulated astronauts. 96% of problems were caught before becoming serious, none were missed, and there were about 1.9 false warnings per healthy astronaut per month.
- Privacy: each astronaut sees only their own twin; management sees only fitness for duty.
- Honesty: all data is synthetic and labelled; thresholds are demo criteria that need medical validation; ORBIT TWIN is a prototype, not a medical device.
